name: Tigecycline
route_note: IV infusion every 12 hours after a loading dose.
targets: 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit (aminoacyl-tRNA A site)

discovery.note: A minocycline derivative with a glycylamido group at position 9 that overcomes common tetracycline efflux and ribosomal-protection resistance. Year GAR-936 (later tigecycline) was first described in the literature, per Wikipedia; the glycylcycline class was reported from 1993.

tagline: Glycylcycline for multidrug-resistant infections, limited by a mortality signal
summary: Tigecycline is the first glycylcycline, a minocycline derivative developed by Wyeth and approved in 2005. It is active against MRSA, VRE, many ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales and Acinetobacter, but higher all-cause mortality in trials restricts it to situations where alternatives are unsuitable.
mechanism: Tigecycline binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and blocks entry of aminoacyl-tRNA into the A site, inhibiting protein synthesis; it binds the ribosome about five times more tightly than older tetracyclines.

Its bulky 9-glycylamido side chain makes it a poor substrate for Tet efflux pumps and helps it escape TetM-type ribosomal protection. It is inactive against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Proteus, which have intrinsic efflux (e.g. MexXY, AcrAB), and plasmid tet(X) monooxygenases that inactivate it have been reported since 2019.
uses: Off-label salvage therapy for carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter and Enterobacterales infections

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Tygacil for complicated skin and intra-abdominal infections.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Tygacil is authorised in the European Union.

history.title: Mortality warning
history.detail: The FDA warns of increased all-cause mortality in a pooled analysis of trials.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: A boxed warning on all-cause mortality is added to the US label.

history.title: tet(X) resistance genes
history.detail: Plasmid-mediated high-level tigecycline resistance genes tet(X3) and tet(X4) are reported in China.

safety.boxed_warning: All-cause mortality was higher in patients treated with tigecycline than with comparators in a meta-analysis of clinical trials; reserve for situations when alternative treatments are not suitable.

facts: Tigecycline's large volume of distribution gives low serum concentrations, a concern for bloodstream infections.
